445/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE II ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM, MANGALURU, DAKSHINAKANNADA,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS MFA, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Ravishankar Shastry, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.P.B.Raju., learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
2.
This is a claimant's appeal.

Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mangaluru in M.V.C No.445/2019 dated 07.01.2021.
3.
This is an admitted case of amputation of right lower limb at the level of knee joint due to the injury sustained by the appellant in a road traffic accident.

As against the claim for Rs.25,00,000/-, the Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.7,54,696/- as compensation and dissatisfied with the same, the claimant has preferred the present appeal.
5. Arguing the matter, Sri.G.Ravishankar Shastry, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries due to the accident and took extensive treatment.
During the course of treatment, there was amputation of right lower limb and thus, the appellant became permanently disabled.

Learned counsel states that though the doctor who assessed the disability appeared before the Court and stated that the disability in respect of whole body is 70%, the Tribunal took the disability as 23% for the reasons best known and calculated the compensation.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submits that the appellant by doing the coolie work was earning an amount of Rs.20,000/- per month and the occupation and earnings of the appellant were established through examining the employer of the NC: 2024:KHC:32203 appellant as PW-3 and also produced the salary certificate.

But the Tribunal taking the notional income as Rs.11,400/- p.m., calculated the compensation which the appellant is entitled to towards loss of future earnings due to the disability and awarded a very meagre amount.

Learned counsel also states that the amount of compensation awarded under other different heads is also on the lower side and therefore, enhancing the same,
justice may be done to the appellant.

Learned counsel also states that for the relevant period Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as Rs.14,000/- per month and the Tribunal ought to have considered at least the said figure but did not do so.

6. On the other hand, the submission that is made by Sri.P.B.Raju, learned counsel for respondent No.2 is that the evidence produced by the appellant himself goes to show that he was earning Rs.11,436/- per month as salary and thus, the Tribunal has rightly took the income NC:
2024:KHC:32203 of the appellant as Rs.11,400/- per month and thus, there is no need for any interference.

7. Learned counsel Sri.P.B.Raju, however contends that the disability assessed by the Tribunal may not be wholly justifiable, but it shall in no case be 70% in respect of whole body as projected by the learned counsel for the appellant.
8. Coming to the aspect of disability in respect of whole body, undisputedly, the appellant sustained crush injury to the right leg and foot.

The contents of Ex.P9- Disability Certificate reveals that as the appellant was unstable haemodynamically, after seeking opinion from surgeons, appellant underwent emergency guillotine's amputation of the right lower limb at the level of knee joint.

He was initially admitted at Father Muller Medical College Hospital, Mangaluru on 26.01.2019,
underwent surgery on the same day and he was discharged on 30.01.2019.

entities.text: Father Muller Medical College Hospital, Mangaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He was readmitted for further management of the stump.
He was followed up regularly in the out NC: 2024:KHC:32203 patient department.
It is not in dispute that the appellant is a coolie by profession.
With amputation of one of the lower limb upto knee, it would be highly impossible for him to attend to his duties with the same efficiency as he was doing prior to the date of the accident.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained and the loss of limb upto knee, this Court is of the view that the disability in respect of whole body has to be taken as 40% for assessing the compensation that is to be awarded under the head of loss future earnings due to permanent physical disability.

9. Coming to the earnings of the appellant by the date of accident, as rightly contended by Sri.P.B.Raju, learned counsel for respondent No.2, as per the contents of Ex.P10, the appellant was drawing monthly salary of Rs.11,436/-.
However, the said document also reveals that the said amount was being earned excluding ESI and PF.
It is also mentioned in the said document that the appellant was earning Rs.200/- to 300/- as overtime NC: 2024:KHC:32203 batta.

Having considered the contents of the said document, this Court is of the view that there is justification in the submission made by Sri.Ravishankar Shastry, learned counsel for the appellant that the notional income has to be taken as Rs.14,000/- per month as taken by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for assessing the compensation.

Therefore, this Court considers desirable to take the Mr Gopal vs Mr P K Mohammed on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118852005/
3 notional monthly income of the appellant as Rs.14,000/-.

sentences.text: By the material that is brought on record, it is clear that the appellant was aged about 41 years by the date of accident.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25% of the actual earnings are required to be added towards future prospects.

12. Likewise, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ NC: 2024:KHC:32203 1298, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '14'.

Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ NC: 2024:KHC:32203 1298

sentences.text:
Thus, with the aforementioned parameters, the loss of future earnings due to permanent physical disability would be as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Notional monthly income 14,000-00 Annual income 1,68,000-00 (14,000 x 12)
Add 25% towards future 2,10,000-00 prospects Apply '14' as multiplier 29,40,000-00 40% being permanent 11,76,000-00 physical disability 13.
This Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation for pain and suffering.
Also the appellant is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards attendant charges, food nourishment and conveyance.
The Tribunal granted Rs.2,15,000/- for artificial limb, which needs no interference.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits at least for a period of six months.

Therefore,
loss of earnings during the laid up period comes to NC: 2024:KHC:32203 Rs.84,000/- (14,000 x 6).
Also this Court considers that the appellant is entitled to Rs.50,000/- for loss of amenities in life.

Thus, the total compensation which the appellant is entitled to is as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and suffering 1,00,000-00 Attendant charges, food, 30,000-00 extra nourishment and conveyance For artificial limb 2,15,000-00 Loss of future income due to 11,76,000-00 permanent physical disability Loss of income during laid 84,000-00 up period Loss of amenities in life 50,000-00  Total 16,55,000-00 Mr Gopal vs Mr P K Mohammed on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118852005/
4 14.

sentences.text:
Thus, in the light of foregoing discussion, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The compensation that is awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mangaluru, through orders in M.V.C No.445/2019 dated 07.01.2021 - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC:32203  is enhanced from Rs.7,54,696/- to  Rs.16,55,000/-.
iii. The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv. The 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. v.
On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.
